chapters.title: Introduction and Talk Agenda
chapters.summary: The speaker introduces himself, his background, and outlines the five topics he will cover about design systems.

chapters.title: Need for Design Systems and Definition
chapters.summary: The speaker explains why design systems are needed due to product complexity and user focus, then defines design systems and lists their elements.

chapters.title: Relating Products via Brand Architecture
chapters.summary: The speaker discusses assessing the current product landscape and presents three brand architecture models that inform design system structure.

chapters.title: Identifying Design System Users
chapters.summary: The speaker distinguishes design system users from end users and identifies various roles such as developers, analysts, product owners, QA, and third parties.

chapters.title: Options for Starting a Design System
chapters.summary: The speaker outlines approaches to start a design system, including using existing systems or building on libraries, noting pros and cons.

chapters.title: Three Design System Approach Options
chapters.summary: The speaker presents three options for building a design system: using open-source libraries, using paid services like Telerik, or creating a custom design system, outlining pros and cons for each approach.

chapters.title: Skills Required for Design System Team
chapters.summary: The speaker details the skills needed for a design system team, including communication, UI design, UX research, accessibility, content design, programming, quality assurance, DevOps, and additional roles like product owner and scrum master.

chapters.title: Recap and Closing Remarks
chapters.summary: The speaker summarizes key decision points for starting a design system, including assessing dependencies, identifying users, choosing an approach, and determining team skills, then introduces himself and provides contact information.
